overall: Board's Purpose 3 executive sessions were proper and the Sep 24 late-added topic and email deliberation claims failed; the Feb 5 and 19 notices and the Feb 19 second-session minutes violated the law, with an order to amend minutes.

allegations.summary: Board allegedly entered executive session on Feb 5, Feb 19, Sep 24 and Oct 15 without a permissible purpose (litigation, Purpose 3).
allegations.key_passage: Thus, we find that the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law by entering executive session under Purpose 3 during the four meetings at issue.

allegations.summary: Meeting notices and open-session announcements for the Feb 5 and Feb 19 executive sessions allegedly were insufficiently detailed.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by including insufficient detail on its February 5 and February 19 meeting notices.

allegations.summary: Notice for the cancelled Jan 29 executive session allegedly was insufficiently detailed.
allegations.key_passage: Because the Board cancelled the January 29 meeting, we find no violation with respect to the sufficiency of the notice for the January 29 meeting.

allegations.summary: Board allegedly deliberated outside an open meeting via email among a quorum on matters within its jurisdiction.
allegations.key_passage: We reviewed these emails and did not find any evidence of deliberation outside of a meeting, because while some Board members expressed opinions on matters before the Board in the emails, none of these emails were sent to a quorum of the Board.

allegations.summary: Board allegedly added a new topic to its Sep 24 meeting notice within 48 hours of the meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Since the Chair only learned on the morning of the meeting that this was a concern needing attention, and that therefore the Board should discuss the promotion of the Deputy Fire Chief, the Chair did not reasonably anticipate this topic 48 hours in advance.

allegations.summary: Not alleged: the minutes of the 8:05 p.m. Feb 19 executive session were reviewed and found to lack a substantive summary of discussion.
allegations.key_passage: We therefore find that the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to draft and approve accurate minutes for the 8:05 p.m. executive session on February 19.

allegations.summary: Allegations that a Board member threatened a complainant and that members misused Town funds, which are not Open Meeting Law matters.
allegations.key_passage: We decline to review those allegations.

allegations.summary: Allegations about notices of meetings held more than 30 days before the first complaint were outside the filing window.
allegations.key_passage: We decline to review any allegations regarding notices of meetings that took place more than 30 days prior to the filing of the first complaint on February 24, as they could have been discovered at the time the meetings took place.

allegations.summary: New allegations raised for the first time in requests for further review, not in the original complaints, were not reviewed.
allegations.key_passage: We decline to review any new allegations contained in the requests for further review that were not included in an Open Meeting Law complaint.

allegations.summary: Allegation that the Board failed to notify a complainant about executive sessions discussing him under the notice rules for subject individuals.
allegations.key_passage: When a discussion fits within multiple executive session purposes, the public body may choose which executive session purpose to utilize.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that a similar future violation may be considered evidence of intent to violate.
Within 60 days of receipt, amend the minutes of the 8:05 p.m. February 19 executive session to include sufficient detail.
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution the Board that a determination by our office of a similar violation in the future may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Open Meeting Law.
